chunks: ʿAlī ibn Ibrāhīm, from his father, from al-Ḥasan ibn Sayf, from his father, from one whom he mentioned, from Abū ʿAbdillāh عليه السلام, who said:

The Messenger of Allah صلى الله عليه وآله addressed the people, then raised his right hand, clasping his palm, then said: “O people, do you know what is in my palm?” They said: “Allah and His Messenger know best.” He said: “In it are the names of the people of Paradise, and the names of their fathers and their tribes, until the Day of Resurrection.”

Then he raised his left hand and said: “O people, do you know what is in my palm?” They said: “Allah and His Messenger know best.” He said: “The names of the people of the Fire, and the names of their fathers and their tribes, until the Day of Resurrection.”
Then he said: “Allah has judged and been just, Allah has judged and been just: a party will be in Paradise and a party in the Blaze.”

key_terms.أَهْلِ النَّارِ: The people destined for the Fire.
key_terms.حَكَمَ اللَّهُ وَعَدَلَ: A declaration that Allah’s judgment is perfectly just.
key_terms.فَرِيقٌ: A party or group among humanity.
key_terms.يَوْمِ الْقِيَامَةِ: The Day of Resurrection when final judgment is manifest.

ai.seo_question: What does this hadith say about Allah’s knowledge of who will enter Paradise and Hell?
ai.summary: This hadith describes the Messenger of Allah صلى الله عليه وآله publicly declaring that the destinies of the people of Paradise and the people of the Fire are known to Allah, down to their lineages and tribes, until the Day of Resurrection. It emphasizes divine knowledge, divine justice, and the ultimate division of humanity in the Hereafter.
